dialogues.speaker: Dusk Keeper
dialogues.text: The windows go violet before the street goes dark. That's usually when I remember I left the broom outside.

dialogues.speaker: Dusk Keeper
dialogues.text: There’s always one petal stuck in the corner of the top step. I sweep the whole street, and that one gets to stay.

dialogues.speaker: Dusk Keeper
dialogues.text: I like the lantern light best on the stair edges. You can see every nick in the stone.

dialogues.speaker: Dusk Keeper
dialogues.text: That black crow sits so still against the dark roof that I only notice it when it calls.

dialogues.speaker: Moonveil shepherd
dialogues.text: If you hear a clack downstairs, that's my loom. If you hear a thump, I've dropped the shuttle again.

dialogues.speaker: Moonveil shepherd
dialogues.text: When I carry a basket up, I set it on the landing and take a breath. Nobody in this house will rush you past a good place to sit.

dialogues.speaker: Moonveil shepherd
dialogues.text: I started a mat for the door. It came out too nice to wipe boots on, so now I'm making a worse one.

dialogues.speaker: Moonveil cartographer
dialogues.text: My map has a mark for every stair and none for the view. I keep meaning to fix that.

dialogues.speaker: Moonveil cartographer
dialogues.text: I tried drawing the whole staircase on one sheet. It looked like a snail. I left it that way.

dialogues.speaker: Moonveil cartographer
dialogues.text: From below you see the trunk. Up here you can watch the branches move one at a time.
